sections.what: Allies in Hope provides HIV-related healthcare and support in Houston. Its programs combine supportive housing, case management, food assistance and prevention services. Housing and practical support aim to make stable daily life and continued care easier for individuals and families.
sections.monitoring: The current homepage reports 285 residents affordably housed, 3,966 patients receiving testing, PrEP or other services and 1,671 pantry participants without an identified reporting period. These may overlap and are not added. Request annual unique households, stable housing duration, completed care and incremental household payments versus other assistance.
sections.qualitative: Current housing programs provide a concrete clinical and resource mechanism. Original returns identify the recipient and comparable annual expense boundaries. Current services include case management addressing barriers beyond medical appointments. Undated housing counts do not establish annual unique households or clinical completion. Incremental utility and disposable-resource gains remain unsupported local hypotheses. HOPWA, Ryan White and other assistance complicate additionality and marginal funding. Original IRS returns identify EIN 76-0073661, formerly AIDS Foundation Houston. Current official donation route was checked; no checkout transaction or restricted payee was verified.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $351.02 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 0.322508 clinical QALYs and 0.132713 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.000285 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $15,979,301. The 285 housed-resident figure is an undated annual reference proxy, mapped by judged .8 distinct-household share and .25 additional annual implementation. Clinical .2 response times .03 utility for one finite year is a weak housing/HIV-care morbidity hypothesis, not measured ART efficacy or mortality. Independent .5 resource success receives $600 net additional housing resources after alternative assistance, taxes and benefit withdrawal; positive overlap .5 then full $75 one-off process burden gives $225 net, while other exposed households lose $75. Union 57 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 11.4; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $15,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Housing subsidies are transfers, not new production. A matched distinct payer/displaced-beneficiary stress prices truly incremental budget or displacement, not a second charge for grants already in annual cost. Public and partner incidence is unknown centrally. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: FY 2024 expense $15,798,878 plus netted event cost $180,423 gives $15,979,301. FY 2023 includes $17,162,291 tax expense, $137,354 event cost and $41,266 donated services removed in Schedule D, totaling $17,340,911. FY 2022 includes $15,083,194 tax expense, $58,837 event cost and $186,492 donated services, totaling $15,328,523. The 2024 revenue-side donated service line is not automatically an expense addback; no expense-side donated services recovered. Unrecognized volunteer and partner costs remain unknown.

model.costScope: Whole recipient recognized annual resources versus narrow housing and linked-care hypothesis; other portfolio and marginal gift unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Houston housing and clinics; .95 local share judgment; multi-state camp/prison activities unpriced
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Existing HOPWA, Ryan White, public housing, other HIV providers, insurance and family support remain baseline
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional stable housing and appropriate continued HIV-related care; undated service counts are not completed causal outcomes
